areas-of-inquiry-music-for-dramatic-impa.d: Areas of Inquiry: Music for Dramatic Impact, Movement and Entertainment
terms: Areas of inquiry
IBDP Music 2020 syllabus organises study around four areas: music for sociocultural and political expression, for listening and performance, for dramatic impact, presentation, entertainment.
Diverse musical material
Coursework requires study of at least four musical contexts; cannot be from same geographical/cultural cluster.
Global influences
Cross-cultural exchange spans Silk Road via Marco Polo (1271-95), West African to Caribbean (transatlantic), Beatles to Indian classical (1965 Norwegian Wood).
Local musical contexts
Personal or community traditions students draw on; required as first lens for global comparison in the exploring component.
Musical cultures
Bruno Nettl's Study of Ethnomusicology 1983 framed music in cultural context as central; Nettl identified 29 issues for the field.
World music label
Coined 1987 at London meeting of independent labels (Globestyle, Cooking Vinyl); marketing category for non-Western traditions.

areas-of-inquiry-music-for-listening-and.d: Areas of Inquiry: Music for Listening and Performance
terms: Audience-performer relationship
Christopher Small's Musicking 1998 reframed performance as a relational social act including listeners.
Concert programming
Curatorial decisions about repertoire order; Joseph Joachim's chronological format in Berlin 1864 influenced modern recitals.
Performance practice
Historically informed performance (HIP) Nikolaus Harnoncourt 1953 Concentus Musicus Wien revived Baroque techniques.
Presenting component
IBDP Music final assessment for performance includes solo/ensemble recording, programme notes and reflective commentary linking to inquiry areas.
Stagecraft and presentation
Visual, gestural and ritual elements; Glenn Gould's elimination of live concerts 1964 highlighted recording vs concert distinction.
Technical aspects of performance
Intonation, dynamic balance, articulation, vibrato control; assessed against stylistic criteria for chosen contexts.

areas-of-inquiry-music-technology-in-the.d: Areas of Inquiry: Music Technology in the Electronic and Digital Age
terms: EDM and laptop performance
Trance, dubstep (UK Skream 2004), brostep (Skrillex 2010); Ableton Live 2001 transformed live electronic performance.
Early experiments
Theremin invented 1920 by Leon Theremin; Ondes Martenot 1928 Maurice Martenot; Trautonium 1929 Friedrich Trautwein.
Elektronische Musik
WDR Cologne studio 1951; Stockhausen's Studie I 1953 and Gesang der Junglinge 1956 used pure sine tones and synthesised sound.
House and techno 1980s
Frankie Knuckles at Chicago's Warehouse 1977-83; Detroit techno trio Juan Atkins, Derrick May, Kevin Saunderson 1985 Cybotron.
Moog synthesizer 1964
Robert Moog's voltage-controlled modular system; Wendy Carlos's Switched-On Bach 1968 best-selling classical album.
Musique concrete
Pierre Schaeffer 1948 RTF Paris; Etude aux chemins de fer assembled recorded sound; founded GRMC studio 1951.
Arrangement techniques
Reharmonisation, reorchestration, metric modulation; Quincy Jones's arrangement of Fly Me to the Moon for Sinatra 1964 exemplary.
Composition processes
Sketching motifs, harmonic experiments, orchestration trials and revision drafts documented in commentary; Beethoven's sketchbooks model practice.
Experimenting component
IBDP Music portfolio task; create musical material through composing, arranging, improvising or producing across multiple contexts.
Improvisation
Spontaneous composition within structure; jazz blues changes and Indian classical alap demonstrate improvised disciplines.
Notation choices
Standard staff notation, lead sheets, tablature, graphic scores (Cornelius Cardew's Treatise 1967), DAW MIDI clips for the digital domain.
Sound production techniques
Multitrack recording (Les Paul 1947), MIDI 1983, Pro Tools 1991, plugin synthesis; transformed music creation in studios.

Afro-Cuban jazz
Dizzy Gillespie and Chano Pozo's Manteca 1947 fused bebop with Cuban clave; later expanded by Mario Bauza and Machito.
Bhangra-pop
Birmingham UK 1980s; Apache Indian's Boom Shack-A-Lak 1993; Punjabi MC's Mundian To Bach Ke 1998 globally remixed.
Jazz fusion 1969
Miles Davis's In a Silent Way February 1969 and Bitches Brew August 1969 fused jazz with rock electricity and modal forms.
K-pop
Lee Soo-man founded SM Entertainment 1995; Seo Taiji and Boys 1992 origin; BTS Dynamite 2020 first all-English Korean No. 1.
Reggaeton
1990s Puerto Rico/Panama; based on Dem Bow riddim from Shabba Ranks 1990; Daddy Yankee's Gasolina 2004 global breakthrough.
World fusion 1980s
Peter Gabriel's WOMAD 1982; Paul Simon's Graceland 1986 with Ladysmith Black Mambazo; Mickey Hart's Planet Drum 1991 (Grammy).
